title.zh: 呼吸器病：消炎、强壮肺组织与灸的持久作用
title.en: Respiratory Diseases: Anti-inflammation, Strengthening the Lung, and Sustained Moxa

summary.zh: 呼吸器病他分两路：急性炎症(喉头炎、气管炎、支气管炎)以反射、诱导旺盛血行、消炎发汗为目的，取风池、大杼、风门、肺俞等颈背穴配尺泽、合谷、外关；慢性病(慢性支气管炎、支气管扩张、肺气肿、喘息、肺结核)则以“加强肺组织细胞之功能”为目的，多灸、久治，并强调摄生。肺炎只作辅助，肺脓疡、声门水肿、气胸等明言非针灸适应证。
summary.en: He splits respiratory disease in two. Acute inflammations (laryngitis, tracheitis, bronchitis) are treated by reflex and induction to boost circulation, reduce inflammation and induce sweat, on neck-and-back points with Chize, Hegu, Waiguan. Chronic disease (chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis) aims to strengthen lung tissue, mostly with prolonged moxa and stress on hygiene. Pneumonia is adjunct only; lung abscess, glottic oedema and pneumothorax are declared not for acupuncture.

takeaways.zh: 急性炎症的目的写得很明确：以反射与诱导旺盛局部或全身血行、消炎，气管炎、急性支气管炎再加“发汗”。喉头炎取风池、液门、鱼际为主，重者加肺俞、手三里、少商刺出血；支气管炎则日针1次，针后频饮热开水以求出汗。
takeaways.en: For acute inflammation his stated aim is boosting local or whole-body circulation by reflex and induction and reducing inflammation, with sweating added for tracheitis and acute bronchitis. Laryngitis: Fengchi, Yemen, Yuji, plus Feishu, Shousanli and Shaoshang bleeding when severe; bronchitis: needle daily and drink hot water afterwards to sweat.

takeaways.zh: 慢性病的目的换成“强壮”：加强肺部组织细胞的功能、旺盛血行、增加营养吸收(慢性支气管炎、支气管扩张)，或促进肺组织新陈代谢以回复呼吸功能(肺气肿)，喉头结核同样以“加强肺脏与喉头组织之细胞活力……增加抗力”为目的。
takeaways.en: For chronic disease the aim becomes strengthening: raise the function of lung tissue cells, circulation and nutrient absorption (chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis), or promote lung metabolism to regain respiratory function (emphysema); laryngeal tuberculosis is likewise aimed at cell vitality, blood flow and resistance.

takeaways.zh: 取穴的骨架：颈背上部(风池、风门、大杼、身柱、肩井)与肺俞是核心——21条中肺俞出现于15条(在16条列有穴位者中)；上肢配尺泽、太渊、合谷、外关；久病咳痰者另取中脘、足三里、丰隆以助消化营养。肺结核明言“食欲不振者，每次针治时，中脘、三里必不可少”。
takeaways.en: The skeleton of point choice is upper neck and back (Fengchi, Fengmen, Dazhu, Shenzhu, Jianjing) with Feishu, which appears in 15 of the 16 entries that list points; arm points Chize, Taiyuan, Hegu, Waiguan; and Zhongwan, Zusanli, Fenglong for long-standing cough and phlegm. For tuberculosis he says Zhongwan and Zusanli are indispensable at every visit when appetite is poor.

takeaways.zh: 针与灸的分工：急性期用针，慢性期靠灸。他说慢性支气管炎“比较用灸法为宜，以其持久性较长”，可灸愈后二三年不发；支气管扩张“久灸较针效为强”；喘息发作时针、停止后用小艾炷灸二三个月；肺结核则针治使热度、盗汗消失、脉搏退到90至以下后才改灸。全章有8条提到灸法。
takeaways.en: Division of labour: needle for the acute phase, moxa for the chronic. Chronic bronchitis is better moxaed for its lasting effect (sometimes no relapse for two or three years); bronchiectasis responds more to prolonged moxa than needle; in asthma needle at the attack then small cones for two or three months; in tuberculosis moxa replaces needle once fever, night sweats and pulse >90 have settled. Eight entries mention moxa.

takeaways.zh: 刺激量因病而异：肺结核体弱神经过敏，“重刺激手术，绝对避免”，背部轻刺、四肢中等，每次不超过8穴；肺炎用26号针浅刺略捻即出；慢性喉头炎、慢支、肺气肿用中刺激(共5条)，而声门痉挛发作时、肋膜炎用强刺激(各1条)；皮肤针用于慢性喉头炎、声门痉挛与水胸。
takeaways.en: Dose varies with the disease. In frail, nervous tuberculosis patients heavy stimulation is absolutely avoided (light on the back, moderate on the limbs, no more than 8 points a visit); pneumonia gets a No. 26 needle inserted shallowly and withdrawn after a light twist. Moderate stimulation is named in five entries; strong stimulation only at a glottic spasm attack and in pleurisy; the skin needle appears in chronic laryngitis, glottic spasm and hydrothorax.

takeaways.zh: 他为针灸划定了边界：肺炎的主要治疗“应由医家用消炎、灭菌之药物”，针灸作辅助；喉头癌、声门水肿、肺脓疡、气胸明言非针灸适应证，肺水肿“不适应用针灸”(数据库把它标作yes，应以原文为准)；肋膜炎中化脓性、出血性、腐败性者亦非适应证；肺结核到二期“必助以药物”。
takeaways.en: He fences off acupuncture: for pneumonia the main treatment belongs to a doctor using anti-inflammatory, germicidal drugs and needling is an adjunct; laryngeal cancer, glottic oedema, lung abscess and pneumothorax are stated not indicated, pulmonary oedema is "not suited" (the database tags it yes; the text governs), and purulent, haemorrhagic or putrid pleurisy is excluded. Second-stage tuberculosis must have drugs added.

takeaways.zh: 肺结核是本章最详细的一条：先解除忧虑，休养营养为主；症状有先后——盗汗发热者以止盗汗为主，发热咯血者先解热，咯血咳嗽者先止血，感冒者先治感冒；不可求速效，不宜每日多穴，好转后隔三四日1次，症状全消后每周1次，钙化后续针二三个月。他明言“肺病以摄生重于治疗”。
takeaways.en: Tuberculosis is the most detailed entry: relieve worry first, rest and nutrition come first; symptoms are ranked (night sweats before fever, fever before haemoptysis, haemoptysis before cough, a cold first); no hope of quick results, no daily multi-point treatment; spaced to every third or fourth day, weekly after symptoms clear, and two to three further months after calcification. "Hygiene outweighs treatment."

takeaways.zh: 预后态度是分级并附危险信号：喉头炎、气管炎、支气管炎多“良”；慢性喉头炎“不易全治”，肺气肿“完全根治则难”；肺炎见高热、皮肤青紫、鼻翼煽动、鼻色淡白多数不治，热退而泄泻、食欲不振、鼻翼煽动者亦不治；肺结核后期多不良。
takeaways.en: Prognosis is graded and comes with danger signs: laryngitis, tracheitis and bronchitis mostly good; chronic laryngitis "not easily cured", emphysema hard to cure completely; in pneumonia high fever with cyanosis, flaring nostrils and a pale nose is mostly fatal, as is falling fever with diarrhoea, poor appetite and flaring nostrils; late tuberculosis mostly poor.

title.en: Respiratory: disease → aim → key points → technique → prognosis

rows: 咳：肺俞、督俞、膏肓、尺泽、太渊；热：大椎、身柱、厥阴俞；盗汗：阴郄、后溪；食欲差：中脘、足三里

rows.en: No. 26 needle strong daily; chronic → small moxa; purulent etc. excluded

rows.en: Dry/serous mostly good; others mostly poor

title.en: Respiratory conditions he declares outside acupuncture

Drugs by a specialist, without delay

caveats.zh: 病名与病理为民国时期的西医概念(如格鲁布性肺炎、肋膜炎、肺结核“传尸”)，机理表述沿用“反射”“诱导”“神经”。肺结核、肺炎等在今日有抗生素与抗结核药，他当时明言药物为主、针灸辅助，不能当作独立疗法。“肺水肿”一条在结构化数据中被标为适应证，而原文明言不适应用针灸，此处以原文为准。
caveats.en: Disease names and pathology are Republican-era Western concepts (croupous pneumonia, pleurisy, tuberculosis), with mechanisms stated as reflex, induction and nerves. Antibiotics and antituberculous drugs now exist; he already treats drugs as primary and acupuncture as adjunct, so this is not a stand-alone therapy. The pulmonary oedema entry is tagged as indicated in the structured data although the text says acupuncture is unsuitable; the text governs here.
